market.summary: The KLCI fell 1.6% to 1,643.96, its lowest close in three months, and broke below the 1,655 floor that had held all month. Banks led the selling (CIMB, RHB, Maybank) as the US 10-year Treasury yield hit a 19-year high and oil stayed above US$100. The monthly trend rule fails more clearly than before. RSI 28 is oversold, so a bounce is likely, but a bounce is not a trend: wait for a close back above about 1,700 (the 10-month average) before buying anything.

notes: Run on Tue 29 Sep, 6.40pm, after the close (TradingView data for 1,134 Bursa stocks; 259 liquid). Volume trend = 10-day average ÷ 60-day average throughout. What changed: (1) The KLCI broke below its 1,655 support to 1,643.96 (−1.6%), led by banks, as US yields hit a 19-year high — the market check fails more clearly. (2) The first data-centre CRESS deal was signed (SD Guthrie/Gamuda/Gentari JV, 680MW solar + battery, RM10bn+ over 21 years), and solar and cable names rallied against the market. (3) Southern Cable broke out: it closed at a record 2.97 on 3.2× volume, above its 2.92 trigger — the first trigger to fire, but the market check blocks buying. (4) Gamuda is 0.4% under its 5.00 high with a new catalyst from the CRESS JV. Follow-ups: Binastra holds its base (2.50); UMS had no fresh Bursa trades; MN Holdings rose to 4.01 on thin volume; Infomina held Monday's jump but hasn't followed through; Powerwell slipped. Defensive stocks (KLK, IOI, Sime Darby, QL, Oriental) held up in the sell-off but aren't in a hot theme, so they're not on the list. Nothing is buyable while the market check fails; the most likely first buys when it turns are Southern Cable (if it holds above 2.91) and Gamuda (on a close above 5.01).

catalysts.title: First CRESS data-centre deal signed — more to follow
catalysts.when: Signed 28 Sep; more expected over Q4 2026
catalysts.theme: Solar / green power for data centres
catalysts.detail: A JV of SD Guthrie (33.5%), Gamuda (33%) and Gentari (33.5%) signed a 21-year CRESS term sheet with a US tech company for at least 680MW of solar plus 4-hour battery storage in Perak, worth over RM10bn of revenue, running from 2029. It confirms the 30% green-power rule is turning into real contracts. HLIB expects Solarvest and Samaiden to sign their first CRESS projects within three months. The installers have already run; the supply chain (cables, switchgear, substations) and the asset owners have not moved as much.

catalysts.title: US yields at a 19-year high, oil above US$100
catalysts.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield is at a 19-year high, reviving Fed tightening fears, and Brent is above US$100 after the US rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal. This is what is pushing the KLCI down; banks and big caps are taking the hit. A fall in yields or a Hormuz de-escalation would be the trigger for a market rebound.
